cards.explanation: The answer is False. The priests and diviners say, “…do not send it away empty, but by all means return it to Him with a guilt offering.” (1 Samuel 6:3) The ark goes back with something beside it. Nobody in this room is saying 'just drop it off and run.'

The answer is a guilt offering, friends. The priests and diviners say to return the ark “by all means… with a guilt offering.” (1 Samuel 6:3) It's the thing that goes along with the ark. They also say what comes next: the Philistines will be healed, and they will understand why His hand has not been lifted.

The answer is five of each, friends. The priests and diviners say, “Five gold tumors and five gold rats… according to the number of rulers of the Philistines.” (1 Samuel 6:4) One of each for every ruler. The same plague had struck both the people and their rulers, so the rulers are counted in.

The answer is glory, friends. The priests and diviners tell them, “Give glory to the God of Israel, and perhaps He will lift His hand from you and your gods and your land.” (1 Samuel 6:5) So glory is part of what they're told to give. It's right there in the same breath as the gold rats.

The answer is True. The priests and diviners ask, “When He afflicted them, did they not send the people out so they could go on their way?” (1 Samuel 6:6) They are pointing to Egypt as a warning. Nobody wants to be the next Pharaoh in somebody's cautionary tale.

The answer is that the calves are taken away and penned up, friends. The text says, “…take their calves away and pen them up.” (1 Samuel 6:7) The men then do exactly that (1 Samuel 6:10). The cows head off to pull the cart while the calves stay penned.

The answer is that it was the LORD who brought the disaster, friends. The priests and diviners say, “If it goes up the road to its homeland, toward Beth-shemesh, it is the LORD who has brought on us this great disaster.” (1 Samuel 6:9) The road is the test, and the cows are the ones taking it.

The answer is chance, friends. The priests and diviners say that if the cart doesn't go that way, “…we will know that it was not His hand that punished us and that it happened by chance.” (1 Samuel 6:9) Chance is the other possibility on the table. It's a two-way test, and one road settles it.

The answer is False. The cows “…headed straight up the road toward Beth-shemesh, staying on that one highway and lowing as they went, never straying to the right or to the left.” (1 Samuel 6:12) They don't wander and they don't turn back. That's some serious commitment from two cows.

The answer is False. The rulers of the Philistines “…followed behind them to the border of Beth-shemesh.” (1 Samuel 6:12) They follow along behind the cows instead of waiting for news. I think I'd have wanted to see it with my own eyes too.

The answer is overjoyed, friends. The people of Beth-shemesh were harvesting wheat in the valley, and “…when they looked up and saw the ark, they were overjoyed at the sight.” (1 Samuel 6:13) They were working, and then the ark came into view. I'd drop my sickle too.

The answer is that they chop up the cart and offer the cows to the LORD, friends. The text says, “The people chopped up the cart and offered the cows as a burnt offering to the LORD.” (1 Samuel 6:14) The cart and the cows both get used right there in the field. Nothing is sent back home.

The answer is False. The text says the Levites “…took down the ark of the LORD and the chest containing the gold objects, and they placed them on the large rock.” (1 Samuel 6:15) The rulers followed the cows to the border and later saw it all (1 Samuel 6:12, 16). The ark is handled by Levites.

The answer is True. The text says, “…when the five rulers of the Philistines saw this, they returned to Ekron that same day.” (1 Samuel 6:16) They see the ark and the offerings, then they go back to Ekron. All of it happens that same day.

The answer is that they looked inside the ark, friends. The text says, “…God struck down some of the people of Beth-shemesh because they looked inside the ark of the LORD.” (1 Samuel 6:19) Seventy men were struck down, and the people mourned. I think this one hurts, so let's let it be heavy.

The answer is Kiriath-jearim, friends. The men of Beth-shemesh send messengers to the people of Kiriath-jearim with this message: “The Philistines have returned the ark of the LORD. Come down and take it up with you.” (1 Samuel 6:21) That's the town they ask. They don't keep it, and they send word.

The answer is Abinadab's, friends. The men of Kiriath-jearim “…took it into Abinadab’s house on the hill.” (1 Samuel 7:1) So the ark ends this passage in a house on a hill. I'd call that a good address for it.
The answer is guard, friends. The text says they “…consecrated his son Eleazar to guard the ark of the LORD.” (1 Samuel 7:1) Eleazar is Abinadab's son. His job is to guard the ark.
